Problem: Attribute "optimize" not supported by some clang compilers and causes warning
Context: repo=cmsis_device_h7, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H7XX, component=None, layer=Other, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=24
Root cause: Hello @pavel-a, Thank you for the report.
Fix: Here: https://github.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H7XX, bug_report, high, enhancement, cmsis, internal bug tracker, system_stm32h7xx, GCC

Technical details:
Here: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/cmsis-device-h7/blob/8f922cdc7cc6de2344e75ddd657889f4ff761790/Include/system_stm32h7xx.h#L88 Description of the problem: [see in the forum](https://community.st.com/t5/stm32cubeide-for-visual-studio/warning-quot-unknown-attribute-optimize-quot-stm32cubeide-vscode/td-p/884776) Proposed change: add check for attribute "optimize" in the #if line above: #if defined(__GNUC__) && __has_attribute(optimize) More to this.... My AI assistant says... > placing __attribute__(optimize) only on the function prototype in a header is not guaranteed to work. > For reliable behavior, you should place the attribute on the function definition in the C file, not just the declaration. > **Why the attribute must be on the definition** > GCC applies optimization attributes at the point where the function is compiled, which is the definition, not the declaration. > If the definition lacks the attribute ..... Then GCC will simply ignore the attribute from the prototype > If this is correct, the #if/#else with attribute "optimize" should be undone (reverted to ver. 1.10.5) in the .h file and the attribute inserted in all variants of system_stm32h7xx****.c on the body of function ExitRun0Mode

Problem: Incorrect values in D1CorePrescTable
Context: repo=cmsis_device_h7, mcu_series=H7, board=NUCLEO-H745ZI, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=low, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=23
Root cause: Duplicate of #12 Hello @radoslav06, Thank you for your report.
Fix: **Describe the set-up** Stm32H7xx **Describe the bug** The D1CorePrescTable is incorrectly initialized to {0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9} and used for both 3-bit and 4-bit prescalers.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, NUCLEO-H745ZI, HAL, bug_report, low, bug, duplicate, good first issue, invalid, cmsis, CANNOT, IMAGE

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** Stm32H7xx **Describe the bug** The D1CorePrescTable is incorrectly initialized to {0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9} and used for both 3-bit and 4-bit prescalers. This issue has been raised several times in different places. However, due to some brain malfunction, the previous issue reported in this repository was closed with the following explanation (#12): > The current D1CorePrescTable[16] is implemented to support both 4-bits dividers like D1CPRE and 3-bits dividers such as D1PPRE, D2PPRE2, D2PPRE1. The thing is - you **CANNOT** implement this table to support both types of prescalers. **How To Reproduce** Open code base, search for D1CorePrescTable. **Additional context** The simplest solution would be to use two separate tables. To explain it further - one table for 3-bit prescalers and one table for 4-bit prescalers. So there is **two** tables in the end. No, you cannot keep single table for both prescalers, I'm sorry. **Other issues describing the problem** https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/cmsis-device-h7/issues/12 https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/issues/301 **Screenshots** Relevant examples describing the 3-bit and 4-bit prescalers values from the reference manual for STMH7xx - in case anyone developing the ST libraries has problem to read the documentation: [IMAGE ATTACHED] [IMAGE ATTACHED]

Key comments:
Duplicate of #12 Hello @radoslav06, Thank you for your report. Could you please share your use case or scenario where you encountered this bug? This will help us understand and address it better. BR, Mohamed Chaker. Hi @radoslav06, I hope you are doing fine. I agree this point is more than tricky, especially if one focuses on the table itself, instead of tracking the **whole trail** from application to drivers. However, once clarified, you will see how all pieces **fit together** and how the whole stuff works **perfectly fine** both for 4-bit and 3-bit prescalers. > [!TIP] > Two points to keep in mind: > 1. The D1CorePrescTable[] table returns the necessary **number of right shifts** in order to achieve the desired clock frequency **division**. > 2. Only a **set of predefined** values are **allowed** as indices of the D1CorePrescTable[] table. > [!IMPORTANT] > For point 2 above to be enforced, it is necessary that the application uses that **set of predefined** values, not arbitrary ones. ---- Let's dive into the details of an existing example, the [RCC Clock Configuration](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeH7/tree/master/Projects/NUCLEO-H745ZI-Q/Examples/RC

issues.issue_title: Is it planned to remove old code and macros?
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: Is it planned to remove old code and macros?
Context: repo=cmsis_device_h7, mcu_series=H7, board=None, component=None, layer=Other, issue_kind=usage_question, severity=high, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=20
Root cause: Hi @KoynovStas, Could you please clarify more what is meant by "an increase in entropy"?
Fix: CMSIS device files (headers) are very large, and changes are periodically made like: https://github.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, usage_question, high, question, cmsis

Technical details:
CMSIS device files (headers) are very large, and changes are periodically made like: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/cmsis-device-h7/commit/e4d57d6edc39f35aced298732829fc2a5e6a8a71 This brings each time a section with Legacy xxx This is almost doubling the code, old + new. Is it planned to remove the old code or is it left for compatibility and will never be removed?. If for compatibility, then if it is with us forever, why introduce new names for the same thing if the old code will 100% not be removed? If at least some plans for a large-scale refactoring that will remove old definitions? I ask because I would like to have synchronized versions of these files with the official repository. But if this refactoring is not planned, we will plan refactoring in our repository, because old/new code with a many of developers leads to an increase in entropy. Thank you.

Key comments:
Hi @KoynovStas, Could you please clarify more what is meant by "an increase in entropy"? Thank you, Sorry for my bad English. I meant that some our developers use the old version, others the new one. This leads to the fact that some code uses old defines, others new ones. If you do not have plans to remove the old code, our Tech Leads would have removed the old code in our repositories. Yes, we will have to update our copy manually when releasing new versions. But this will force everyone to write driver code with one version of definitions. Hello @KoynovStas, The legacy code is maintained for compatibility reasons and will not be removed. Developers have the discretion to choose which version to use. However, we strongly recommend utilizing the new code for any new development. Thank you. Thank you for the official response.

issues.issue_title: Pseudo-random behavior of GCC start-up template when main() returns
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: Pseudo-random behavior of GCC start-up template when main() returns
Context: repo=cmsis_device_h7, mcu_series=H7, board=NUCLEO-H723ZG, component=None, layer=Other, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=low, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=15
Root cause: I had a cursory look at some different stm32 mcu's startup code assembly, it appears that this is done this way across the startup code of more STM32 families; the nonsensical "bx lr" and the missing __libc_fini_array() call is also in the F4 startup code.
Fix: Board: NUCLEO-H723ZG Compiler: arm-none-eabi-gcc (Arch Repository) 14.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, NUCLEO-H723ZG, bug_report, low, bug, good first issue, cmsis, internal bug tracker, GCC, cmsis_device_h7, startup_stm32h723xx, Reset_Handler

Technical details:
Board: NUCLEO-H723ZG Compiler: arm-none-eabi-gcc (Arch Repository) 14.1.0 The GCC start-up assembly template for the H723xx [(see here)](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/cmsis_device_h7/blob/13ba9da797a30e1563a8795f974425fb26dd0457/Source/Templates/gcc/startup_stm32h723xx.s) contains the following code at the end of Reset_Handler: /* Call static constructors */ bl __libc_init_array /* Call the application's entry point.*/ bl main bx lr Usually, main is assumed not to return. However, if it does, the next instruction BX LR will jump to the address stored in the link register. This address will usually be the return address for the last sub-routine call inside main. So, this instruction will jump back into main to a more or less random location. In my particular case, this location was close to the end of main, and execution continued through to the end of main where it pop-ed a value of zero into the program counter. This then triggered a hard fault, because zero is not a thumb mode address, and the default hard fault handler (an infinite loop) was entered. Of course, one can debate about the desired behavior if main returns, but I think we can agree the current behavior is not it. One approach would be to replace BX LR with an infinite loop, similar to the GCC start-up templates for the H5 series. See for example this snippet below (taken from [here](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/cmsis_device_h5/blob/9a778e0f162bd21200647adafb922d50b2c60f81/Source/Templates/gcc/startup_stm32h563xx.s)): /* Call static constructors */ bl __libc_init_array /* Call the application's entry point.*/ bl main LoopForever: b LoopForever One could also consider throwing in a call to __libc_fini_array() after main and before the infinite loop for symmetry.

Key comments:
I had a cursory look at some different stm32 mcu's startup code assembly, it appears that this is done this way across the startup code of more STM32 families; the nonsensical "bx lr" and the missing __libc_fini_array() call is also in the F4 startup code. The H5 startup code has an infinite loop after return from main() -- but no call to _libc_fini_array(). It would be best to homogenize this across all families, I think. That would take a sweep across a bunch of repositories. In general, the behavior when returning from main() should be documented. If the choice is made to not touch the current implementation (for fear of breaking stuff, for example), I'd like to see a clear statement somewhere in the documentation that returning from main() triggers undefined behavior. I wouldn't favor that approach, but it's better than having UB and *not* documenting it. Hello @0xa000, Your point seems very relevant. It has been forwarded to our development teams. I will keep you informed. ST Internal Reference: 192331 Hi @0xa000, Issue fixed in the frame of release **1.10.7**, as you can see from the code snippet below. https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/cmsis-device-h7/blob/8f922c

Problem: Missing linker files for GCC & ARM
Context: repo=cmsis_device_h7, mcu_series=H7, board=NUCLEO-H723ZG, component=None, layer=Other, issue_kind=usage_question, severity=medium, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=14
Root cause: Hello @abudden, Thank you for your contribution.
Fix: **Describe the set-up** * The board: Nucleo-H723ZG * IDE: GCC (with cmake) **Describe the bug** In the folder "[Source/Templates](https://github.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, NUCLEO-H723ZG, usage_question, medium, enhancement, wontfix, cmsis, IDE, GCC, cmsis_device_h7, IAR, STM32H723

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** * The board: Nucleo-H723ZG * IDE: GCC (with cmake) **Describe the bug** In the folder "[Source/Templates](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/cmsis_device_h7/tree/master/Source/Templates)" there are folders for each compiler. Within these are linker files for those compilers. In the [IAR linker folder](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/cmsis_device_h7/tree/master/Source/Templates/iar/linker), there are linker files for a whole host of microcontrollers, including the STM32H723. In the [GCC](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/cmsis_device_h7/tree/master/Source/Templates/gcc/linker) and [ARM](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/cmsis_device_h7/tree/master/Source/Templates/arm/linker) linker folders, there are far fewer and the STM32H723 is one of the ones missing. The [startup code for GCC for the H723](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/cmsis_device_h7/blob/master/Source/Templates/gcc/startup_stm32h723xx.s) is present [in the folder above](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/cmsis_device_h7/tree/master/Source/Templates/gcc), so it seems strange that a corresponding linker file would not be included (or instructions on how to convert the provided IAR ICF linker file to GCC format). **How To Reproduce** 1. Go to repository 2. Look for the GCC linker file for an STM32H723ZG

Fix: **Describe the bug** For the following devices STM32H723/725/730/733/735 the definition of DBGMCU_APB1HFZ1_DBG_TIM24_Pos is incorrect: #define DBGMCU_APB1HFZ1_DBG_TIM24_Pos (24U) It should be changed to: #define DBGMCU_APB1HFZ1_DBG_TIM24_Pos (25U) For STM32H733 only also FMC_SDCMR_MODE_2 should be fixed from: #define F
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H723, bug_report, high, bug, cmsis, internal bug tracker, DBGMCU_APB1HFZ1_DBG_TIM24_Pos, STM32H733, FMC_SDCMR_MODE_2, FMC_SDCMR_MODE_Pos

Technical details:
**Describe the bug** For the following devices STM32H723/725/730/733/735 the definition of DBGMCU_APB1HFZ1_DBG_TIM24_Pos is incorrect: #define DBGMCU_APB1HFZ1_DBG_TIM24_Pos (24U) It should be changed to: #define DBGMCU_APB1HFZ1_DBG_TIM24_Pos (25U) For STM32H733 only also FMC_SDCMR_MODE_2 should be fixed from: #define FMC_SDCMR_MODE_2 (0x3UL << FMC_SDCMR_MODE_Pos) /*!< 0x00000003 */ to: #define FMC_SDCMR_MODE_2 (0x4UL << FMC_SDCMR_MODE_Pos) /*!< 0x00000004 */

Key comments:
Hello @carlo-dev-git, I agree with you on the first point. I will pass it on to the development team for correction, However, regarding the second point, my stance differs from yours, as detailed in the reference manual rm0468 ![image](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/cmsis_device_h7/assets/113367897/77c9eb89-d9ae-4f55-9dc9-cb2718396102) The mode 2 setting in the FMC_SDCMR register is correctly positioned at 3, as indicated in the definition found in the tm32h733xx.h file. ![image](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/cmsis_device_h7/assets/113367897/6f9d8338-24f9-4661-8a87-87fd810d7f53) Rania ST Internal Reference: 177832 Hi Rania, I think you are confusing the bit number with the bit mask: (0x3UL << FMC_SDCMR_MODE_Pos) means 0b0011 which is definitely not MODE[2] bit. (0x4UL << FMC_SDCMR_MODE_Pos) means 0b0100. To confirm my statement, please check the header files of other micros. The following code is taken from stm32h743xx.h: /****************** Bit definition for FMC_SDCMR register *******************/ #define FMC_SDCMR_MODE_Pos (0U) #define FMC_SDCMR_MODE_Msk (0x7UL << FMC_SDCMR_MODE_Pos) /*!< 0x00000007 */ #define FMC_SDCMR_MOD

issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: Incorrect __CM7_REV and some missing values in device headers
Context: repo=cmsis_device_h7, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H742, component=None, layer=Other, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=5
Root cause: ST Internal Reference: 166097 Fixed in commit acfdbb7a81c43cb7106285da16ae6b9b2e4d879e
Fix: **Describe the set-up** I'm reporting this for the STM32H742/743/750/753 family as I am most familiar with them, but it looks like this applies to all other H7 devices.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H742, bug_report, medium, bug, cmsis, internal bug tracker, errata_sheet, CPUID, FC27, cmsis_device_h7, ARM-

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** I'm reporting this for the STM32H742/743/750/753 family as I am most familiar with them, but it looks like this applies to all other H7 devices. **Describe the bug** The __CM7_REV macro indicates that the revision of the M7 core is r1p0, but it's actually r1p1 according to the [errata](https://www.st.com/resource/en/errata_sheet/es0392-stm32h742x743xig-st32h750xb-and-stm32h753xi-device-errata-stmicroelectronics.pdf#page=8) and the CPUID register on a physical device (0x41**1**FC27**1**). I imagine it's a carry over from older F7 devices. Making things more confusing, the datasheet and reference manual do not list the revision and old versions of the errata had a different incorrect value listed (r0p1). https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/cmsis_device_h7/blob/v1.10.3/Include/stm32h742xx.h#L213 The headers also seem to be missing a few definitions (__VTOR_PRESENT, __FPU_DP, and __DTCM_PRESENT) that are present in the template from the included version of CMSIS. https://github.com/ARM-software/CMSIS_5/blob/5.6.0/Device/_Template_Vendor/Vendor/Device/Include/Device.h#L101-L111
